attendance.heading: Attendance Policy

sources.text:
Attendance Policy:  
Each student is expected to attend all classes, tutorials, and practical sessions and to participate 
in all evaluation components. A 10% weight is assigned to assessment linked to attendance and 
participation. To this end, a small surprise quiz will be conducted in the tutorial class. The scores 
in surprise quizzes linked to attendance and participation will be considered in the final score. 
This score will be considered only for students with a minimum attendance of 50% in the 
lecture and tutorial classes separately. For students with attendance less than 50% in either 
the lecture or tutorial class, zero marks will be assigned, irrespective of the  scores in the 
surprise quizzes attempted.

sources.text:
Course Plan 
 
Module 1: Vapor Power Cycles 
 
Learning Objectives 
 To analyze ideal Rankine cycle for a vapor power plant using T•s plot and evaluate thermal 
efficiency by applying first law and second law of thermodynamics. 
 To evaluate performance of Rankine cycle considering isentropic efficiencies of turbine and 
pump. 
 To represent the Rankine cycle processes on the Mollier diagram (enthalpy•entropy chart). 
 To analyze reheat Rankine cycle for a vapor power plant using T•s plot and evaluate its 
performance by applying first law of thermodynamics. 
 To evaluate performance of regenerative Rankine cycle using feed water heaters. 
 To study boilers their mountings and accessories. 
 
Learning Strategy: 
 
Topics Text book 
Chap/Sec 
Carnot cycle deficiencies, Simple vapor power cycle, Ranking Cycle, Actual  
vapor power cycle, Mean temperature of heat addition. Techniques for 
efficiency improvement, Reheat and Regenerative cycles with open & closed  
feed water heaters. 
Combined cycle power plant and its thermodynamics. Combined Heat and  
Power.

Learning Objectives 
 To analyze ideal Rankine cycle for a vapor power plant using T•s plot and evaluate thermal 
efficiency by applying first law and second law of thermodynamics. 
 To evaluate performance of Rankine cycle considering isentropic efficiencies of turbine and 
pump. 
 To represent the Rankine cycle processes on the Mollier diagram (enthalpy•entropy chart). 
 To analyze reheat Rankine cycle for a vapor power plant using T•s plot and evaluate its 
performance by applying first law of thermodynamics. 
 To evaluate performance of regenerative Rankine cycle using feed water heaters. 
 To study boilers their mountings and accessories. 
 
Learning Strategy: 
 
Topics Text book 
Chap/Sec 
Carnot cycle deficiencies, Simple vapor power cycle, Ranking Cycle, Actual  
vapor power cycle, Mean temperature of heat addition. Techniques for 
efficiency improvement, Reheat and Regenerative cycles with open & closed  
feed water heaters. 
Combined cycle power plant and its thermodynamics. Combined Heat and  
Power. 
 
10, TB1

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description:  
The course introduces students to concepts and nuances of Mechanical Engineering Design. Content includes 
materials, standards and design of machine elements and application of scientific principles, technical knowledge, 
and imaginative skills to be developed in a student. The machine elements covered are Shafts, Screw fasteners, 
Welded joints, Springs, Brakes & Clutches, Bearings and Gears. 
The Tutorial classes of the course will be mainly used for assisted problem solving, consultation and evaluation. 
 
 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course:  
To prepare a student of mechanical engineering to apply theory and practice of Design of Mechanical Elements. 
It is an introductory course laying foundation on design ground rules, application of strength of material principles, 
selection of components, and selection of materials for a given application.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description:  
Introduction to manufacturing systems, forecasting, life cycle concepts,  facility location and la yout planning, 
aggregate and batch  production planning, scheduling, inventory control, material requirement  planning, and 
enterprise resource planning, just -in time and lean manufacturing, total quality management, supply  chain 
management and Industry 4.0. 
 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
The objective of this course is to impart important decision making processes and analytical tools in design, planning 
and control of manufacturing / service processes. At the end of the course the students shall be able to establish routes 
and schedules for work that will ensure the optimum utilization of men, materials and machines in a manufacturing / 
services. 
• Familiarize fundamental concepts in production / operations management 
• Understand the decision making process in design, planning and control of manufacturing / service systems 
• Develop skills for decision making in conversion process / manufacturing systems

sources.text:
Make-up Policy: It will be as per the institute rules. Only genuine cases will be considered.
No makeup will be provided for the quizzes under any circumstances.
Quizzes: There will be quizzes based on the objective/subjective type questions during the
tutorial hours. The best four out of five quizzes will be taken for grading. Tentative quiz dates
are: 25th August 2025, 8th September 2025, 22nd September 2025, 27th October 2025, and
10th November 2025. If there are any changes to quiz dates, they will be communicated in
advance. No makeup will be provided for these quizzes under any circumstances.
Minimum Passing Marks: The passing marks for this course will be determined based on one
of the two criteria: 30% of the median of the post-comprehensive examination score or 20% of
the average of the first three top scorers. The lower value between these two criteria will be
considered as a passing mark in this course.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
Course Description:
The internal combustion engine (IC) is a heat engine that converts chemical energy in a fuel into
mechanical energy, usually made available on a rotating output shaft. This is one of the dominating areas
in prime movers. These engines are often used for the propulsion of a vehicle (i.e., automobile, truck,
locomotive, marine vessel, or aeroplane), and other applications include stationary engines to drive
generators or pumps and portable engines for things like chain saws and lawnmowers, etc. This course
will introduce the students to system-level design concepts and the workings of internal combustion
engines. Furthermore, electric mobility has become an essential part of the energy transition. This course
focuses on the fundamentals of the technology behind electric vehicles. It will cover the contents such as
the working principle of electric vehicles and delve into its key components, e.g. motors and power
electronics, battery technology, charging technologies and future trends in the development of electric
vehicles. 
Scope and Objective of the Course: This course has been designed to make the students familiar 
with internal combustion engines and electric and hybrid electric power trains.

mechanical energy, usually made available on a rotating output shaft. This is one of the dominating areas
in prime movers. These engines are often used for the propulsion of a vehicle (i.e., automobile, truck,
locomotive, marine vessel, or aeroplane), and other applications include stationary engines to drive
generators or pumps and portable engines for things like chain saws and lawnmowers, etc. This course
will introduce the students to system-level design concepts and the workings of internal combustion
engines. Furthermore, electric mobility has become an essential part of the energy transition. This course
focuses on the fundamentals of the technology behind electric vehicles. It will cover the contents such as
the working principle of electric vehicles and delve into its key components, e.g. motors and power
electronics, battery technology, charging technologies and future trends in the development of electric
vehicles. 
Scope and Objective of the Course: This course has been designed to make the students familiar 
with internal combustion engines and electric and hybrid electric power trains.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
I. Course Description: 
Introduction to data mining, clustering, classification & association, sequence analysis, regressions method, 
decision trees, machine learning, neural networks, SVM for engineering and manufacturing applications, data 
mining for product design, applications of data mining in production, planning and scheduling, data mining for 
defect identification, process and quality control, application of data mining in maintenance, data analysis for 
machine and manufacturing process monitoring, introduction to cyber physical systems, introduction to big 
data handling and big data analytics.  
II.     Scope and Objective of the course: 
The primary focus of this course is on application of data mining methods in mechanical sciences and 
engineering. Following are the details objectives of this course: 
• Understanding the fundamental of data mining. 
• Building mathematical foundation for data mining. 
• Knowledge of data capturing to minimize the information losses. 
• Understanding of patterns in data, data classification and clustering. 
• Knowledge of application of identified patterns in data in fields like in-processing monitoring, machine 
monitoring, defect analysis, machine and maintenance scheduling etc. 
• Understanding of different prediction methods based on the data processing. 
• Understand the difference between artificial intelligence, machine learning and deep learning.  
• Knowledge of which data mining methods should be used for what type of data. 
• Understanding the concept of big data in mechanical and manufacturing domain and how to handle it.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description: 
This course introduces the necessity, classification, operating principles, and applications of various energy 
storage technologies used in modern energy systems. Mechanical, thermal, electrochemical, electrical, and 
chemical energy storage systems will be discussed with emphasis on their design, operation, performance 
characteristics, advantages, limitations, and practical applications in electric vehicles, renewab le energy 
integration. The course also covers emerging storage technologies including advanced battery systems, 
supercapacitors, hydrogen energy systems, and phase change material-based thermal storage systems. 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
The objective of this course is to provide students with a strong understanding of energy storage 
technologies and their role in sustainable energy systems. The course covers fundamental thermodynamic, 
electrochemical, and mechanical aspects of energy storage systems along with their design considerations, 
performance evaluation, safety issues, and practical applications. The course also aims t o familiarize 
students with recent advancements, technical challenges, economic considerations, and future prospects of 
modern energy storage technologies. The course also introduces Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) as a 
simulation tool for the design, analysis, and performance evaluation of energy storage s ystems, with 
emphasis on thermal management and flow behavior. 
3. Text Books (T.B.): 
• T.B. 1: Robert A. Huggins, Energy Storage: Fundamentals, Materials and Applications, Springer, 2nd 
Edition, 2016. 
• T.B. 2: Reddy, Linden’s Handbook of Batteries, McGraw-Hill Education, 3rd Edition, 2011. 
4. Reference Books (R.B.): 
• R.B. 1: Luisa F. Cabeza, Advances in Thermal Energy Storage Systems: Methods and 
Applications, Elsevier Science & Technology, ProQuest Ebook Central, 2014.  
• R.B. 2: Godula-Jopek, Agata, Walter Jehle, and Joerg Wellnitz, Hydrogen Storage Technologies: new 
materials, transport, and infrastructure, John Wiley & Sons, 2012. 
• R.B. 3: Sandeep A. Arote. Electrochemical Energy Storage Devices and Supercapacitors: An Overview, 
Institute of Physics Publishing, ProQuest Ebook Central, 2022.

sources.text:
1.  Course description: 
This is a first-level course offered to advanced first degree and higher degree students to understand 
the essential concepts in compressible flows. The course contents include Introduction to Gas 
Dynamics, Basic equations for compressible flow, Flow with friction and heat addition, Normal shock, 
Quasi one-dimensional flow, Oblique shock, Prandtl-Meyer Flow, Potential equation for compressible 
flow, Linearized flow solution, and Hypersonic flows.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
Course Description:
This elective course introduces the fundamental principles and emerging applications of microfluidics.
This is one of the dominating areas in prime movers. The course emphasizes both theoretical foundations
and practical insights relevant to microscale fluid behavior, fabrication methods and devices.
Scope and Objective of the Course:
The scope of this course spans across fundamental science, device engineering, and emerging real-world
applications at the micro- and nano-scale. This course provides a comprehensive understanding of
microscale fluid dynamics, and control principles central to microfluidic systems. The course objectives
are to understand the basics of microfluidics and the physics governing microfluidic flows and interfaces,
to explore various microfabrication techniques suitable for fluidic devices and to analyze and understand
the microfluidic systems applications in various engineering domains.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
Course Description:
This elective course introduces the fundamental principles and emerging applications of microfluidics.
This is one of the dominating areas in prime movers. The course emphasizes both theoretical foundations
and practical insights relevant to microscale fluid behavior, fabrication methods and devices.
Scope and Objective of the Course:
The scope of this course spans across fundamental science, device engineering, and emerging real-world
applications at the micro- and nano-scale. This course provides a comprehensive understanding of
microscale fluid dynamics, and control principles central to microfluidic systems. The course objectives
are to understand the basics of microfluidics and the physics governing microfluidic flows and interfaces,
to explore various microfabrication techniques suitable for fluidic devices and to analyze and understand
the microfluidic systems applications in various engineering domains.

sources.text:
1. Course Description:
Introduction to tensors, tensor algebra and tensor calculus. Kinematics of deformation (displace-
ment, velocity , deformation gradient, material and spatial ﬁeld descriptions, description of local
deformation, linearized kinematics, kinematic rates), left & right Cauchy-Green deformation ten-
sor, Cauchy-Lagrangian strain tensor. T raction and stress (ﬁrst Piola-Kirchhoff stress, second
Piola- Kirchhoff stress, Biot stress etc). Mechanical conservation and balance laws (conservation
of mass, conservation of linear momentum, conservation of angular momentum, conservation of
energy , work done by stresses and the principle of virtual work, BVP , IVP , calculus of variation).
Constitutive relations (constraints on constitutive relations, frame indifference, objectivity , material
symmetry , constitutive models for linearly elastic, hyperelastic solids and ﬂuid ﬂows).
2. Scope & Objective of the Course:
This course will provide an introduction to continuum mechanics. It aims to develop in students
the foundational mathematical rigor needed to understand advanced topics in solid and ﬂuid me-
chanics.

sources.text:
1. Course description: The course introduces smart materials and smart structures through their physical 
mechanisms, characteristic responses and engineering use. Major topics include piezoelectric ceramics 
and polymers; one-way, two-way and magnetic shape-memory alloys; electro- and magnetorheological 
fluids; magnetostrictive and electrostrictive materials; and fibre -optic and FBG sensors. Basic 
modelling is embedded within the relevant material modules using physically interpretable equations 
and response curves. Applications i nclude sensing, actuation, vibration control, damping, structural -
health monitoring, energy harvesting and intelligent devices.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description:  
Basic concepts of probability and probability distribution, Standard probability distribution, Sampling and 
Sampling Distributions, Confidence intervals, testing significance, Statistical tolerance, Various types of 
control charts, Statistical process control techniques, Defect diagnosis and prevention, Basic concepts of 
reliability, Reliability design evaluation and control, Method of applying total quality  management into 
production process. 
 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
This course presents an exposition to the modern thoughts on quality and related practices. The  principles 
and techniques for quality control, based on statistical methods and the procedures for quality  assurance are 
covered. Tools for quality engineering and quality management are dealt in detail. Concepts of reliability and 
methods to improve product and systems reliability are also covered. The course is tailored to enable students 
to become successful managers in a sustained manner, thereby provide support to the business houses in their 
never-ending quest for quality.

Course Description: 
Principles, thermodynamic analysis, load estimates  and design of various refrigeration and air 
conditioning systems for comfort and industrial applications. Theoretical or experimental 
investigation of refrigeration and air-conditioning problems. 
 
Scope and Objective of the Course: 
The course is designed to give a comprehensive understanding of the theoretical principles and 
practical aspects of the refrigeration and air -conditioning. The basic governing principles and 
refrigeration cycles, thermodynamic analysis and the associated components analysis and design 
of refrigeration systems will be covered. The comprehensive understanding of the design and 
implementation of the air-conditioning processes and systems will also be discussed.

1. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
This course is designed to provide an in -depth and holistic understanding of the technology and 
principles under lying modern robotics. Over the years, the demand for human -like machines 
capable of replacing or assisting humans in diverse and challenging work environments has grown 
significantly due to reasons such as efficiency, precision, safety, and the need to op erate in 
hazardous conditions. In response to this need, the field of robotics has rapidly evolved and 
established itself as one of the most critical and promising areas of engineering for the future. 
The course aims to build a strong interdisciplinary fou ndation for students, focusing particularly on 
the mechanical aspects of robotic systems while integrating relevant knowledge from electronics,

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description:
Fundamental concepts, matrix algebra and gaussian elimination, one-dimensional problems, trusses,
two-dimensional problems using constant strain triangles, axisymmetric solids subjected to ax-
isymmetric loading, two-dimensional isoparametric elements and numerical integration, beams
and frames, three-dimensional problems in stress analysis, scalar field problems, dynamic con-
siderations, pre-processing and post processing.
2. Scope & Objective of the Course:
The scope of the course is limited to an introduction to FEA as applied to elasticity problems in
solid and structural mechanics. This course will train the students to analyze real-world structural
mechanics problems using the finite element method. Students will be introduced to the mathe-
matical basis of finite element analysis, on which nearly all structural analysis software are built.
The objectives of the course are:
CO1. Understand strong and weak formulations, methods of weighted residuals Rayleigh-Ritz
method.
CO2. Understand the finite element method procedure, which converts a given boundary value
problem into a set of algebraic linear equations that can be solved using computer.
CO3. Understand the implementation of FEM for linear analysis of 1D and 2D problems of solid
mechanics and heat transfer.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description: Design principles of machine tools; stiffness and rigidity of separate construction 
elements and their combined behaviour under load; design of stepped and stepless drives; electrical, 
mechanical and hydraulic drives; design of bearings and slideways; mach ine tool controls; machine tool 
dynamics; recent developments in machine tool design 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: The Course is intended to focus the student’s attention on the 
concepts of design, analysis and features of different types of machine Tools, different machine elements to 
make a machine tool and new concepts in machine tool engineering. 
Course Objectives (CO): 
CLO1. To advance the theoretical and fundamental understanding of machining processes 
CLO2. To understand the concept of hydraulic and mechanical transmissions employed in machine tools  
CLO3. Calculation of machining time of various operations 
CLO4. To understand the design of gear boxes for stepped control of speed and feed in machine tools 
CLO5. To understand the design solution of different machine tool elements 
CLO6. To understand the functioning and operation of numerically control machine tools.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
I. Course Description: 
 
Introduction to neural networks, approximation properties, backpropagation, deep network training, 
regularization and optimization, convolution neural networks, recurrent neural networks, attention models, 
transformers, neural architecture search, federated learning, meta-learning, applications in time series modeling 
and forecasting, online (incremental) learning.  
II.     Scope and Objective of the course: 
 
This course is designed to impart the knowledge to understand the basics of deep learning and their applications 
in mechanical engineering. The objectives of this course are: 
• Understand and explain the architecture, training, and optimization techniques used in deep neural 
networks. 
• Apply deep learning techniques to solve problems in mechanical engineering domain. 
• Analyze the performance and behavior of deep learning models. 
• Evaluate the strengths and limitations of different deep learning architectures and techniques for 
mechanical engineering specific problems. 
• Critically assess the latest advancements in deep learning. 
III. Textbook and Reference Books:  
T1. Aston Zhang, Zack C. Lipton, Mu Li, Alex J. Smola : Dive into Deep Learning, Cambridge

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description: 
This course provides a comprehensive foundation in industrial robotic systems and robot control. Topics 
include principles of robot kinematics, statics, dynamics, and control; rigid body motion and coordinate 
transformations; rotation matrices, Denavit -Hartenberg parameters forward and inverse kinematics; Jacobian 
analysis, workspace and singularity analysis; trajectory planning and motion optimization; robot statics and 
dynamics using Euler –Lagrange and Newton –Euler formulations; control  system f or robot, independent joint 
control, computed torque control, and force control; end -effector and gripper design for robotic manipulation 
and precision assembly; sensor -integrated robotic systems; collaborative robotics; robotic work -cell 
implementation; and case studies and applications of industrial robots in intelligent manufacturing 
environments. 
 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
This course provides fundamental, theoretical, and applied knowledge of industrial robotics and robot control 
with a strong emphasis on hands-on learning and industry-oriented applications. The course develops a rigorous 
foundation in robot kinematics, dynamics, motion planning, and control required for the modelling, analysis, 
and operation of industrial robotic manipulators. 
Students will gain practical exposure to industrial robotic systems used in modern manufacturing environments 
for robotic manipulation, precision assembly, collaborative robotics, and intelligent production systems. 
Laboratory sessions and project -based learning will focus on robotic manipulator programming, trajectory 
generation, end-effector design, sensor-integrated robotic systems, and robotic work -cell implementation using 
industrial-grade platforms. 
Course Outcome: 
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to: 
 
CO1 Apply principles of robot kinematics, dynamics, and control to model and analyze industrial robotic 
manipulators. 
CO2 Design and implement motion planning and control strategies for industrial robotic tasks such as pick-and-
place, assembly, and material handling. 
CO3 Design and deploy sensor-integrated robotic work cells for real-world manufacturing applications with 
closed-loop control. 
CO4 Demonstrate hands-on proficiency and industry readiness by solving practical robotics problems through 
labs, projects, and industry-led sessions.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description  
This course provides students with a comprehensive understanding of molding methods used for plastic components in 
the manufacturing of electronic components. It will introduce s tudents to different molding techniques  used for plastic 
components, and equipment , process considerations, and applications in the electronics industry.  The second module 
provides an overview of the different materials , characterization and testing  procedures, and environmental safety 
considerations in the electronic industry. In the third and fourth modules, students will be exposed to  different plastic-
moulding processes used in the fabrication of electronic components. The last module will provide basic design aspects 
related to injection mould, compression mould, transfer mould, and blow mould for fabricating electronic components. 
Through a strong focus on experimental exposure and industry case studies, students will develop practical insights into 
advanced manufacturing systems used in the electronics industry.   
 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course  
This course introduces theoretical, analytical, and practical knowledge of plastic materials used in the electronic industry, 
as well as  the manufacturing methods for  plastic components. It provides students with basic knowledge of advanced 
casting methods for fabricating plastic components for the electronics industry. It enables learners to understand the 
principles of various advanced casting methods, the casting machines used, the mechanisms of these processes, the 
parameters involved , and  basic design aspects related to mould . Additionally, this course provides industrial/practical 
exposure to industrial component development and various application areas with case studies.  
3. Course Outcomes  
 
CO No. Course Outcome 
CO1 Develop an understanding of the moulding processes and testing techniques involved in the fabrication 
of plastic components in the electronics industry.   
CO2 Selection of appropriate materials for the electronic industry.  
CO3 Design and fabricate different plastic components using moulding processes.  
CO4 Acquire b asic design skills related to injection mould, compression mould, transfer mould, and blow 
mould. 
CO5 Demonstrate hands -on proficiency and industry readi ness by solving practical electronic component 
fabrication problems through labs, projects, and industry-led sessions.

Course Title : Computer Aided Design & Additive Manufacturing

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description
This course provides a comprehensive understanding of advanced computer-aided design
(CAD) and digital product development techniques used in modern engineering design and
manufacturing. It covers geometric modelling of parametric curves, surfaces, and Non-Uniform
Rational B-Splines (NURBS), along with geometric transformations, mass property evaluation,
and product data exchange standards for seamless CAD interoperability . The course intro-
duces Design of Experiments (DoE) for design optimisation and provides extensive hands-on
training in basic and advanced Geometric Dimensioning and T olerancing (GD&T) based on
the ASME Y14.5 standard using commercial CAD software. Students will also explore the
fundamentals of generative design, topology optimisation through industrial case studies, and
the principles and applications of additive manufacturing, enabling them to design innovative,
lightweight, and manufacturable engineering products.
2. Scope & Objective of the Course

sources.text: Course Title              : Theory of Elasticity & Plasticity
Course Title              : Theory of Elasticity & Plasticity

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description: The course has wide-ranging application in Engineering structures, Machine tool 
structures, metal forming, and cold working. The studies deal with the determination of stresses and 
displacements in common structural forms beams, shafts, shells etc. subjected to external forces. The 
course covers basic theory of elasticity, 2 -D and 3-D problems of elasticity, Theories of plastic flow, 
Flow of ideally plastic and strain hardening metals, and theory of metal forming processes.  
2. Course Level Objectives:  The course is for higher degree students to prepare them in applying the 
theory on some problems of practical and design interest. The students will be able to appreciate 
underlying meaning of material and structural behavior under complex loading conditions. Students 
are also encouraged to do assignments using the ANSYS/ABAQUS package to solve problems of 
elasticity and plasticity to compare the analytical solutions.  
CO1: Understand the concept of stress and strain in situations where large deformations are involved. 
CO2: Appreciate the governing differential equations that describe a general boundary value problem 
in elasticity. 
CO3: Solve the general elasticity boundary value problems with various boundary conditions using 
methods of complex variable techniques 
CO4: Appreciate the concept of yielding and yield criteria. Yield surface and normality rule, 
associated flow rule

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
Course Description:
This elective course introduces the fundamental principles and emerging applications of microfluidics.
This is one of the dominating areas in prime movers. The course emphasizes both theoretical foundations
and practical insights relevant to microscale fluid behavior, fabrication methods and devices.
Scope and Objective of the Course:
The scope of this course spans across fundamental science, device engineering, and emerging real-world
applications at the micro- and nano-scale. This course provides a comprehensive understanding of
microscale fluid dynamics, and control principles central to microfluidic systems. The course objectives
are to understand the basics of microfluidics and the physics governing microfluidic flows and interfaces,
to explore various microfabrication techniques suitable for fluidic devices and to analyze and understand
the microfluidic systems applications in various engineering domains.

Course Description:
This elective course introduces the fundamental principles and emerging applications of microfluidics.
This is one of the dominating areas in prime movers. The course emphasizes both theoretical foundations
and practical insights relevant to microscale fluid behavior, fabrication methods and devices.
Scope and Objective of the Course:
The scope of this course spans across fundamental science, device engineering, and emerging real-world
applications at the micro- and nano-scale. This course provides a comprehensive understanding of
microscale fluid dynamics, and control principles central to microfluidic systems. The course objectives
are to understand the basics of microfluidics and the physics governing microfluidic flows and interfaces,
to explore various microfabrication techniques suitable for fluidic devices and to analyze and understand
the microfluidic systems applications in various engineering domains.

syllabus.heading: Course description

sources.text:
1. Course description: The course introduces smart materials and smart structures through their physical 
mechanisms, characteristic responses and engineering use. Major topics include piezoelectric ceramics 
and polymers; one-way, two-way and magnetic shape-memory alloys; electro- and magnetorheological 
fluids; magnetostrictive and electrostrictive materials; and fibre -optic and FBG sensors. Basic 
modelling is embedded within the relevant material modules using physically interpretable equations 
and response curves. Applications i nclude sensing, actuation, vibration control, damping, structural -
health monitoring, energy harvesting and intelligent devices.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description:  
Basic concepts of probability and probability distribution, Standard probability distribution, Sampling and 
Sampling Distributions, Confidence intervals, testing significance, Statistical tolerance, Various types of 
control charts, Statistical process control techniques, Defect diagnosis and prevention, Basic concepts of 
reliability, Reliability design evaluation and control, Method of applying total quality  management into 
production process. 
 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
This course presents an exposition to the modern thoughts on quality and related practices. The  principles 
and techniques for quality control, based on statistical methods and the procedures for quality  assurance are 
covered. Tools for quality engineering and quality management are dealt in detail. Concepts of reliability and 
methods to improve product and systems reliability are also covered. The course is tailored to enable students 
to become successful managers in a sustained manner, thereby provide support to the business houses in their 
never-ending quest for quality.

syllabus.heading: Course description

sources.text:
1. Course description: The field of Digital Very Large -Scale Integrated Circuits has gone 
through dramatic evolutions and changes. This course builds on the previous course MEL G621 
VLSI DESIGN. It is intended to give a detailed knowledge and experience in the design of 
advanced VLSI circuits and chips in todays and future nano-scale CMOS technologies. Design 
of high -performance digital systems, failure issues, and remedies of problems. Topics will 
focus on current issues, including: wiring resistance and how to deal with it, power and Ground 
noise and regulation, clock (or asynchronous) system design and how to minimize clocking 
overhead, high-speed I/O design, energy minimization, including leakage control. Major VLSI 
design challenges are followed by careful treatment of several versatile digital and mixed 
analog-digital circuit building blocks frequently utilized in VLSI chips.

syllabus.heading: Course description

sources.text:
1. Course description: The field of Digital Very Large -Scale Integrated Circuits has gone 
through dramatic evolutions and changes. This course builds on the previous course MEL G621 
VLSI DESIGN. It is intended to give a detailed knowledge and experience in the design of 
advanced VLSI circuits and chips in todays and future nano-scale CMOS technologies. Design 
of high -performance digital systems, failure issues, and remedies of problems. Topics will 
focus on current issues, including: wiring resistance and how to deal with it, power and Ground 
noise and regulation, clock (or asynchronous) system design and how to minimize clocking 
overhead, high-speed I/O design, energy minimization, including leakage control. Major VLSI 
design challenges are followed by careful treatment of several versatile digital and mixed 
analog-digital circuit building blocks frequently utilized in VLSI chips.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description:  
Historical perspective; Processing overview; Crystallography of semiconductors; Defects in semiconductors; 
Clean room; Wafer- growth; cleaning; oxidation; epitaxy; wet and dry etching; lithographic process; diffusion; 
ion implantation; deposition of films using CVD, and PVD techniques; device and circuit fabrication; Process 
Integration: Passive components, Bipolar Technology and MOSFET Technology, Fabrication of advanced 
VLSI devices; System on chip; Future trends and Challenges: 
Laboratory components: Simulation of key fabrication processes using CAD tools; Demonstration of basic 
FEOL/BEOL fabrication processes; Fabrication and testing of electronic devices. 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
 
The objective of the course is not only to introduce the basic principles involved in IC fabrication , but 
also, to discuss processing technology. Fabrication of integrated circuits is a joint venture by electrical  
engineers, chemical engineers, materials scientists, and physicists. This interdisciplinary course builds bridges 
across various disciplines.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description:
We will study the fundamental structures of VLSI Systems at the lowest levels of system abstraction,  
namely those associated with the direct application of VLSI devices to particular problems of interest.  
The broad topics of coverage includes Principles of operations of CMOS transistors used as a digital  
switch and various other topologies used in Digital VLSI Design, Logic implementation strategies and  
performance characterization of the VLSI circuits, Low Power Design, different clocking strategies,  
symbolic layout systems, CMOS subsystems design and Memory modules.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description:
We will study the fundamental structures of VLSI Systems at the lowest levels of system abstraction,  
namely those associated with the direct application of VLSI devices to particular problems of interest.  
The broad topics of coverage includes Principles of operations of CMOS transistors used as a digital  
switch and various other topologies used in Digital VLSI Design, Logic implementation strategies and  
performance characterization of the VLSI circuits, Low Power Design, different clocking strategies,  
symbolic layout systems, CMOS subsystems design and Memory modules.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description: Physics and properties of semiconductor - a review; Semiconductor transport model, 
modeling of metal-semiconductor junctions, pn homojunction and heter ojunctions, bipolar transistor, JFET, 
MESFET, HEMT and; MOS capacitor, modeling of MOSFET, scaling issues, and recent trends in advanced 
MOSFETs 
 
Laboratory Components: Modeling and simulation of silicon-based devices with TCAD software. I-V, C-V 
measurement of MS and MOS junctions. 
 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
This course is designed to provide the basic physical concepts behind microelectronic devices and imparts 
information on modeling of these devices for their use as circuit elements in integrated circuits. It will provide 
the ability to deal with advanced concepts of microelectronic devices along with non -ideal effects in devices 
with an attempt to establish an introduction to research methodology.

syllabus.heading: Course description

sources.text:
1. Course description: VLSI design flow, Simulation based verification, Test bench 
tools and languages, System Verilog, Formal verification, Impact of scaling, wafer 
sort or probe test, DC and AC parametric test, Test economics and product quality, 
Fault models and types; Fault  equivalence, Fault dominance, Automated test 
generation for combinational logic (fault simulation, ATPG, D -algorithm, PODEM, 
FAN); Test generation for sequential logic; Testability  measures, Design for 
testability (Full -scan and partial scan, BIST,  Boundary scan), Delay fault; Analog 
and mixed signal circuit testing, Memory test, IDDQ test

attendance.heading: Attendance Policy

sources.text:
Attendance Policy: Each student is expected to attend all classes, tutorials, and practical sessions and 
to participate in all evaluation components. A 10% weight is assigned to assessment linked to 
attendance and participation. To this end, a small surprise quiz will be con ducted in the tutorial class. 
The scores in surprise quizzes linked to attendance and participation will be considered in the final 
score. This score will be considered only for students with a minimum attendance of 50% in the 
lecture and tutorial classes separately. For students with attendance less than 50% in either the 
lecture or tutorial class, zero marks will be assigned, irrespective of the scores in the surprise quizzes 
attempted.

sources.text:
Tutorial Instructor : Prof. Sharad Shrivastava,Prof. J.S Rathore, Prof. Sachin Belgamwar, 
Prof.  Anuj Sharma, Prof. Kushagra Tiwari 
Introduction: 
Fundamental principles of mechanics, introduction of mechanics of deformable bodies, force and 
moment transmitted by slender members (2D truss, frame, beam), stress and strain, stress strain - 
temperature relations, torsion of circular member, stress and def lection due to bending, buckling 
of columns, theories of failure.

2. Scope & Objective of the Course:
The objective of the course is to impart practice of machine drawing and solid modeling using a
conventional 3D CAD software. The course will also cover Geometric Dimensioning and T oleranc-
ing (GD&T).

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description:  
The course introduces students to concepts and nuances of Mechanical Engineering Design. Content includes 
materials, standards and design of machine elements and application of scientific principles, technical knowledge, 
and imaginative skills to be developed in a student. The machine elements covered are Shafts, Screw fasteners, 
Welded joints, Springs, Brakes & Clutches, Bearings and Gears. 
The Tutorial classes of the course will be mainly used for assisted problem solving, consultation and evaluation. 
 
 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course:  
To prepare a student of mechanical engineering to apply theory and practice of Design of Mechanical Elements. 
It is an introductory course laying foundation on design ground rules, application of strength of material principles, 
selection of components, and selection of materials for a given application.

sources.text:
Instructor-in-charge : PRATEEK KALA 
 
1. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
This course is intended to a comprehensive knowledge of the technology related to Mechatronics and Automation. The 
necessity of integrating and embedding electronics and microprocessor into mechanical systems have been long felt, 
due to rapid progress in microprocessor computer based technology, in domestic products to manufacturing systems. 
Mechatronics is a recently defined engineering field that builds on the traditional mechanical engineering studies, 
combines it with technologies from the electrical, electronics, computer and control fields, using techniques such as 
simultaneous engineering to provide solutions in manufacturing applications. Also, mechatronics has been applied 
to manufacturing and other industrial automation: robotic automation found in car automated production lines, such 
as welding, and  assembly line in computer integrated manufacture etc. Thus, the manufacturing system is greatly 
enhanced by the application of mechatronics.

systems.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description:  
Significance of metal machining and machine tools, Geometry of cutting tools, Mechanics of 
machining processes and analysis, Role of cutting fluids and properties,  Abrasive machining 
processes and analysis, Economics of machining,  Regulation of speed and feed rates in machine 
tools, Design of machine tool structures, Guideways, Spindles, Design of cutting tools for various 
machine tools, Jigs and Fixtures 
 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course:  
This course is designed to enrich theoretical, analytical as well as practical knowledge about metal 
cutting techniques  and various  machine tools used in manufacturing. The course  include 
undrerstanding of  important factors associated  with machining  such as what is the mechanics of 
cutting, why cutting fluid is necessary in metal removal, and how abrasive machining processes are 
different from tool-based cutting processes. The course also includes  design aspect of cutting tools, 
machine parts (structure, spindles, jigs-fixtures) would be explored to comprehend the knowledge of 
machine tools.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description: 
Fundamentals of continuous improvement, value -added and waste elimination, elements of lean production: 
small lot production, setup time reduction, maintaining and improving equipment, pull production systems, 
focused factories and group technologies, work cells and cellular manufacturing, standard operations, quality 
of design, systems for eliminating defects, simplified production planning and control systems: scheduling for 
smooth flow, synchronizing and balancing process, planning and control in pull production, b eyond the 
production systems: managing the supply chain, activity based costing, performance measurement. 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
 
In factories around the globe, Toyota consistently raises the bar for manufacturing, product development and 
process excellence. The result is an amazing business success story: steadily taking market share from price - 
cutting competitors, earning far more profit than any other automaker, and wining the praise of business 
leaders worldwide. With a market capitalization greater than the value of General Motors, Ford and Chrysler 
combined; Toyota is the world’s most profitable automaker. Toyota’s well known “secret weapon” is lean 
manufacturing – the revolutionary approach to business processes that it invented in the 1950’s and has spent 
decades for perfecting. Today business around the world is attempting to implement Toyota system to maintain 
competitive advantage. But are they? 
 
The course explains Toyota’s unique approach to Lean manufacturing, that drive Toyota’s  quality and 
efficiency obsessed culture. You will valuable insights that can be applied to any organization and any 
business process, whether in services or manufacturing. You will discover how the right combination of long- 
term philosophy, processes, people and problem solving can transform your organization into a lean, learning 
enterprise – the Toyota way. 
 
At the end of this course, the students will be able to understand the importance of lean manufacturing / The 
Toyota Way as a strategic weapon, th e students will be able to understand the World –Class power of the 
Toyota way

sources.text:
Instructor In-charge   : SRIKANTA ROUTROY 
    :Amit Bhomia(RS) 
 
1. Scope & Objectives of the Course: 
The course provides students with the opportunity to get clarity and insight into the 
application of various supply chain modelling approaches and empirical analysis for 
evidence driven decision making in supply chain. The objectives of the course are: 
• To introduce concept of decision making on the basis of multiple experts’ opinion on 
various different supply chain problems, practices and strategies. 
• To develop skill sets to analyze the qualitative data with a focus on empirical modelling 
for data driven decisions in supply chain. 
• To develop model for life cycle analysis for measuring environmental sustainability in 
supply chain. 
• To understand and analyse the various aspects of digital supply chain, cultural 
implications and their impact on supply chain performance.

syllabus.heading: Course description

sources.text:
1. Course description: 
Human-centered innovation, Design thinking (DT), consumer needs, creativity for new ideas/products (or re-
design products) for solving problems, DT process’ stages– inspiration, ideation & implementation, DT tools 
– stakeholder map, user persona,  Hook’s canvas, empathy map, AEIOU model, PoV, problem  statement, 
stakeholder wish list, SCAMPER, prototyping & testing, MVP or minimum viable product, business 
model/canvas & business ecosystem. The pedagogical focus will be on hands-on approach to learning. 
 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
The objective is to develop knowhow and skills that promote human-centered approach to innovation through 
design thinking (DT). It will aim to develop understanding of consumer needs & using creativity for new 
ideas/products (or re -design products) for solving problems. Course will also help understand prototyping, 
testing of new ideas & see the context of the larger ecosystem. Focus will be on understanding design 
thinking concept and tools for effective innovations that can solve consumers’ needs holistically. Design 
Thinking process is laid across 3 stages - inspiration, ideation and implementation for new product 
development or re -design & concepts like MVP or minimum viable product, business model/canvas & 
business ecosystem will be also covered. The pedagogical focus will be on hands-on approach to learning.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description: 
The course provides to the students: 
1. An insight into the scientific & analytical methods, techniques and tools of economics 
2. A precise and comprehensive coverage of fundamental concepts in economics 
3. Suitable real world applications & examples to expose him/her to possibilities of implementing concepts in business and economic practices and polices 
4. Approach to integrate different aspects of a firm’s economic decisions within the firm’s framework as well as find & understand connections with the 
macroeconomic environment 
 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
This course aims at providing an overview of comprehensive coverage of fundam ental concepts, analytical tools understanding economics of business decision 
making for a profitable and sustainable status in dynamic business environment. While the primary unit of analysis is firm, t he coverage of this course would 
enable finding & understanding connections of firms’ decisions with its industry and the macroeconomic environment at large.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description: This basic course in marketing is designed to familiarize students with the strategic 
and tactical decision making process in marketing that deals with the fundamental goal of creating, 
communicating and delivering value to the customer. This requires a professional knowledge of market 
drivers, competitors’ capabilities, technological trends and the market dynamics of value. The focus will be 
on the imbibing the skills of uncovering market opportunities by asking certain strategic questions. 
 
 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: On successful completion of this course, participants will be able to 
critically analyze and intelligently draw inference about the marketing strategies of organizations. Through an 
intensive assignment an effort will be made to develop the necessary skills for crafting a typical marketing  
plan grounded in real world data. Finally, awareness of tools available to m arketing managers to facilitate 
planning and decision-making would be one of the gains from the course. 
Students are encouraged to bring some of the topical issues of contemporary concern in marketing to 
the classroom for discussion . Students will also be expected to imbibe path -breaking classic marketing 
literature in a group setting through group discussions for a sound academic base. A number of journal articles 
will be discussed in this course to give the course its academic rigor. The course pedagogy lays special emphasis 
on “learning by doing ” through regular discussion of 6-7 Harvard Business Review cases as well as through a 
group marketing project assignment.

structure, and change management, while also covering the strategic role of HRM in attracting, 
developing, motivating, and retaining talent through recruitment and selection, training and 
development, performance management, employee e ngagement, compensation, and talent 
management.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description 
This course introduces students to the practical usage of databases, emphasizing SQL. As big data problems 
become more prevalent  for businesses, this module introduces the basics of databases. After successful 
completion of the course, students will be able to learn why database management is essential, analyze the data 
requirements of a business scenario and represent these requirements utilizing entity -relationship (ER) 
diagrams, translate an ER diagram into normalized tables for  a relational database management system, and 
write simple and relatively complex data retrieval queries. Students will learn how to extract valuable insights 
from databases through data analytics powered by SQL.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description 
This course introduces students to the practical usage of databases, emphasizing SQL. As big data problems 
become more prevalent  for businesses, this module introduces the basics of databases. After successful 
completion of the course, students will be able to learn why database management is essential, analyze the data 
requirements of a business scenario and represent these requirements utilizing entity -relationship (ER) 
diagrams, translate an ER diagram into normalized tables for  a relational database management system, and 
write simple and relatively complex data retrieval queries. Students will learn how to extract valuable insights 
from databases through data analytics powered by SQL.

Variables & data types, operators, conditional statements, iteration  statements, functions, 
Objects, and classes for Python; Data structures – vectors, matrices, lists, tuples, dictionaries, data 
frames, Packages: using existing packages and creating new packages, Data loading: from CSV, MS 
Excel, JSON & SQL databases Data wrangling: describing, summarizing, manipulating, and handling 
missing values of da ta in data frames; perform an  operation such as delete values, find unique 
values, drop duplicate values, grouping, and performing loop operations over columns  or rows; 
merging data frames; handling categorical data; handling time-series data, handling text data, web 
scraping, and handling images. Basics of version control using Github. Primary languages are R and 
Python.

Course Title : Deep Learning for Business

syllabus.heading: Course description

sources.text:
1. Course description: This course offers an introduction to deep learning and its practical relevance in 
business contexts. It covers foundational concepts such as neural networks, linear and logistic 
regression using neural architectures, deep neural networks, hyperparameter tuning , and advanced 
models like CNNs, RNNs, LSTMs, GANs, and deep reinforcement learning. The course blends 
theoretical understanding with hands -on applications to solve real -world business problems. It also 
highlights the challenges and limitations of deep learning methods in practice. 
 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: The course aims to equip students with foundational and practical 
knowledge of deep learning algorithms and their applications in solving business challenges.  The 
course emphasizes:  
a. Understanding core deep learning architectures and techniques 
b. Translating business problems into machine learning tasks 
c. Developing, training, and tuning deep learning models using appropriate tools 
d. Applying deep learning to solve business challenges 
e. Utilizing TensorFlow and Keras libraries on Google Colab to implement and explore deep learning 
algorithms 
f. Recognizing the limitations, ethical concerns, and interpretability issues of deep models in 
business decision-making 
g. Engaging in a group-based project, where students apply deep learning techniques to some real-
world business problems

world business problems

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description: 
The course imparts skills on big data in analytics using Apache Spark. At the end of the course, students are 
expected to apply concepts of big data and big data architecture on huge volumes of real time data, and develop 
product or solutions development. 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
Apache Spark is the tool taught for handling the concepts of big data. All the illustrations are done on native 
Spartk, and with Python API for Spark i.e., PySpark. Students may use R Spark API for submission of 
assignments.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description:  
  Supply chain performance, Descriptive analytics, Supply chain forecasting, studying holt, winter and 
ARIMA models, Supply chain segmentation. Single period and multi -period inventory modeling, Multi -
echelon inventory models, Network flow mo dels, Distribution planning, Sales, & Operations planning, 
Vehicle routing problems, Simulation in supply chain risk assessment 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
 
 Supply chain analytics is amalgamation of supply chain management and data analytics. In  this 
course you would be given basics and tool/techniques of data analytics with the domain of SCM. 
Students will be exposed to fundamental theories in business practice, and limitations and 
difficulties of supply chain management theories in solving real problems. The basic objective of 
this course is to help students develop the skill found in competent supply chain manager as well 
as analyst.

sources.text:
Course Instructors: Prof. Achint Nigam (achint.nigam@pilani.bits-pilani.ac.in) 
Course Description (Scope and Objective): This course equips students with the analytical frameworks, methods, 
and tools needed to make evidence-based marketing decisions across the customer lifecycle. It introduces the role 
of marketing analytics in supporting strategic and operational decisions,  distinguishing business intelligence, 
analytics, and data science, and communicating insights through dashboards and data -driven storytelling. 
Students will apply analytical techniques to core marketing problems including customer segmentation and 
positioning, product and pricing analytics, market mix modeling, customer journey analysis, customer experience, 
retention and lifetime value, digital marketing measurement, and attribution. The course covers methods such as 
cluster analysis, multidimensional scaling, conjoint analysis, regression, price elasticity modeling, forecasting and 
diffusion models, principal component analysis, logistic regress ion, A/B testing, ANOVA, Bayesian networks, 
and optimization. 
The course also examines the growing role of artificial intelligence, machine learning, text and image analytics, 
recommender systems, personalization, and responsible generative AI in marketing. Emphasis is placed on 
practical interpretation and managerial application of results using tools such as Microsoft Excel, Power BI, DAX, 
and Python/R. By the end of the course, students will be able to translate marketing data into actionable insights, 
evaluate marketing performance, and develop data-informed recommendations for products, customers, channels, 
and brands.

1. Course Description: 
This course provides an introduction to both the theory and the practice of revenue management and pricing , 
Fundamentals of price theory, Segmentation and price differentiation, Break - even analysis, Price sensitivity 
and willingness -to-pay, Empirical estimations of price -response functions, Price optimization, Markdown 
optimization, The hedonic pricing model, Revenue Management, Monte Carlo simulation for pricing decisions, 
Conjoint analysis for pricing decisions. 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: The objectives of this course are: (1) To make you acquainted with the 
concept of pricing and how data can help in setting the right price for the organization. This will be done 
primarily through lectures, class discussions and assigned readings.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
Course Description: 
All organizations need to research their markets periodically and employ various elements of 
marketing research process viz. problem definition, development of an approach to the problem, 
research design formulation, fieldwork & data collection, data prepa ration & analysis and finally 
report preparation and presentation. 
The emphasis of the course is proportionately focused on foundational concepts, methodology & 
techniques, and marketing research applications. A number of cases will be assigned for discussion 
in the class. The course pedagogy lays special emphasis on “ learning by doing ” and a project 
assignment in this course characterizes this orientation. 
1. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
To impart necessary foundational concepts, methodologies and tools/techniques for role of 
a market researcher. That role envisages generation of actionable, reliable and accurate 
information to identify various marketing problems viz. demand forecasting, 
segmentation, targeting, positioning, new product deve lopment etc. and find their 
effective solutions.

1. Brief Course Description: 
The course introduces students to the applications of different techniques of Statistics, Analytics, 
and machine learning to solve financial problems. The students will be exposed to understanding 
the characteristics of financial data, solving  univariate and multivariate time series based 
forecasting problems for prices and returns, problems on portfolio allocation, rebalancing and 
optimization, Security performance analytics, trading strategies, Application of clustering and 
text mining in fin ancial problem solving. The course will be a practical hands -on course which 
would be delivered in excel/Python. 
 
2. Scope and Objectives of the Course: 
This course aims at discussing the role of data and analytics i n financial decision making, 
understanding the statistical properties of financial data. The student should be able to price 
different securities by understanding their characteristics and using different statistical and 
machine learning techniques. The student should also be able to create optimal portfolios catering 
to the requirements of different user groups and evaluate the portfolios using different metrics. The 
course also aims to discuss some of the most prominent applications of Analytics in Financ e like 
Credit Scoring, Debt collection, Sentiment Analysis, Trading strategies

Instructor(s)   :  Prof. Daitri Tiwary ( daitri.tiwary@pilani.bits-pilani.ac.in) 
Office hours for consultation : Prof. Daitri Tiwary: Monday 3PM to 4PM    
Class timing:   : Tuesday, Thursday & Friday, 12-12:50 PM 
  
1. Scope of the Course: 
This course introduces students to the fundamentals of financial derivatives and their applications in 
managing financial risk. It covers the basic concepts of forwards, futures, options, and swaps, along with 
their trading mechanisms, pricing principles, and hedging strategies. Students will also gain an introductory 
understanding of option pricing models, including the Binomial and Black–Scholes models, and explore the 
use of derivative instruments in equity, currency, interest rate, and fixed-income markets. 
 
2. Course Objectives: 
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able: 
1. To explain the fundamental concepts, features, and applications of financial derivatives, including 
forwards, futures, options, and swaps. 
2. To distinguish between different derivative instruments and their use in managing market, currency, 
and interest rate risks. 
3. To apply basic option trading, hedging, and pricing techniques to analyze financial risk management 
scenarios. 
4. To demonstrate the use of introductory derivative pricing models, including the Binomial and 
Black–Scholes models, for valuing financial derivatives. 
5. To evaluate the suitability of derivative instruments for hedging and investment decisions in equity, 
currency, interest rate, and fixed-income markets.

Instructor-in-charge : Prof. Saurabh Chadha (Dept. of Management) 
 
 
 
1. Scope and Objectives of the Course: 
 
 
A key component of financial management is the act of calculating and managing a company's 
value. In essence, managers work to increase the value of their companies in two ways: by 
increasing the firm's productivity through internal (or organic) growth and by making wise 
acquisitions that play to the company's core competencies. It follows that practically every 
significant business choice is decided by asking, "What is it worth?" This course's main goal is 
to arm you with the conceptual foundation, logical framework, and intuitive reasoning needed 
to make thoughtful decisions on company value. 
This course's emphasis is on asses ing the value of the entire enterprise and valuing stock in a 
company. For our study, we'll depend on the income and market approaches of financial 
valuation. The course begins by presenting a brief framework on the rules regulating financial 
statements and changes that are frequently needed to capture the underlying company reality 
because financial statements serve as the foundation for all types of valuation methodologies. 
We will use spreadsheet for building the financial model of a company. 
This course will be most helpful to students who are either pursuing a career in investment 
banking, corporate finance, venture capital, entrepreneurship, or business consulting or who 
would like to do so. The course also has a broader appeal to people who want to improve their

sources.text:
1. Course description: 
There will be three weekly classes.  Class time will be devoted to lectures, role-plays, exercises, 
questionnaire, case discussions and videotapes. Lectures will provide analytical concepts that 
will integrate the readings and serve as useful framework for a richer understanding of cases 
and role-plays. Role-plays, cases and videotapes provide the "application" aspects of this 
course. These participative activities are further enhanced by rigorous self-review (through 
Journal, Follow-up Report and Critique). Tests and Project will provide an opportunity to test 
comprehension of the theory and readings. 
 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
 
People Analytics is the application of data science and information technology in the domain of 
Human resource management. The present course is designed to progress the understanding 
of the role of data-driven decisions about people's issues in an organization. This emerging 
discipline signifies the strategic role of HR function in the contemporary organizations. 
However, with the advent of analytics, it has evolved into a holistic function taking care of all 
people related aspects at the workplace, not only traditional HR operations. It serves as a key 
driver in pursuit of sustainable competitive advantage for organizations by leveraging data 
driven practices for an improved decision making. Grounded on 4Ts principle: Task, Theory, 
Technique, and Technology; the course integrates underlying theories and principles, and data 
analytical tools and techniques to drive business objectives. The course is structured to equip 
students with hands-on experience on analytical softwares to track, maintain, retrieve, 
analyze, and interpret HR data (e.g., staffing, skills, performance ratings and compensation 
information) to contribute to business outcomes. This will serve the twin purpose of elevating 
the students’ understanding on nuances of analytics in organizations, which will aid in 
students’ value addition and employability. 
The learning objectives of the course are as under:  
 This course introduces the student to the theory, concepts, and business application of 
human resources research, data, metrics, systems, analyses, and reporting.

names: their impact on supply chain performance.

sources.text:
Instructor In-charge  :  SRIKANTA ROUTROY (Pilani Campus) 
    Brijesh Kumar Singh(RS) 
    PHANEENDRA KIRAN CHAGANTI (Hyderabad Campus) 
 
1. Scope & Objectives of the Course: 
The course provides students with the opportunity to get clarity and insight into the 
application of various supply chain modelling approaches and empirical analysis for 
evidence driven decision making in supply chain. The objectives of the course are: 
• To introduce concept of decision making on the basis of multiple experts’ 
opinion on various different supply chain problems, practices and strategies. 
• To develop skill sets to analyze the qualitative data with a focus on empirical 
modelling for data driven decisions in supply chain. 
• To develop model for life cycle analysis for measuring environmental 
sustainability in supply chain. 
• To understand and analyse the various aspects of digital supply chain, 
cultural implications and their impact on supply chain performance.

makeup.heading: Make-up Policy

sources.text:
9. Make-up Policy: Make-up is not given as a routine and is considered for only regular students. It is solely dependent 
on the "genuineness" of the circumstance under which a student fails to appear in a scheduled evaluation component. 
The students must discuss such a situation with the IC and get prior permission for make-up. In case of urgent medical 
emergencies, the students must ensure that the message reaches IC as soon as possible. It is particularly difficult to 
arrange make-up for the lab sessions due to the limited availability of lab instructors who are Ph.D. scholars.  Reasonable 
attendance in theory and practical sessions will be a decisive factor in allowing make-up. The decision of the IC in all 
matters shall be final.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description: Basic techniques of pharmaceutical analysis, data handling and analysis, sources of 
error in analysis. The analytical methods would comprise various titrimetric methods, such as acid -base, 
complexometric, non-aqueous, oxidation-reduction, precipitation, conductometric; physical and instrumental 
analysis such as gravimetric, polarography, nephelometry, amperometry, turbidometry, potentiometry; 
chromatographic separations such as TLC, column, ion-exchange, extraction methods such as gel -filtration, 
fractionation processes, analysis of metallic and non -metallic elements; water content, as well as evaluation 
of drug constituents in various pharmaceutical preparation.  
2. Scope and Objective of the Course:  The objective of this course is to provide students with knowledge 
of basic principles of quantitative analytical chemistry necessary for use and interpretation of pharmaceutical 
methods of analysis especially those methods official in the Indian, United S tates and British 
Pharmacopoeias. 
3. Textbooks (TB):  
1. A.H. Beckett and J.B. Stenlake. “Practical Pharmaceutical Chemistry” 4th ed., Part 1 & 2 
4. Reference Books (RB):  
1. Fundamentals of Analytical Chemistry, 9th Edition, Douglas A. Skoog, Donald M. West, F. James, Holler, Stanley 
R. Crouch; Brooks Cole; Brooks/Cole, Cengage Learning  
2. Vogel’s Textbook of Quantitative Chemical Analysis, 6th Edition, J. Mendham, R.C. Denney, M. Thomas, David J. 
Barnes, B. Sivasankar; Pearson Education

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description:  This course focuses upon the physiological and  medical significance of important 
biomolecules along with their use as drug targets. The course also elaborates the role of vitamins as prosthetic 
groups of enzymes and enzyme kinetics and regulation. The course deals with the understanding of chemical 
structures, biochemical reactions  metabolic pathways related to carbohydrates, lipids, nucleic  acids and 
protein synthesis and diseases arising from defects in these pathways. 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: The aim of this course is to describe and explain all biochemical 
processes of living organisms and their interactions with their networking both in health and disease 
conditions.

1. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
 
This course deals with the study of important classes of drugs that are listed below. Various aspects like 
structure, properties, therapeutic and pharmaceutical importance and the uses of drug molecules of both 
natural and synthetic origin will be covered. Study of physiochemical properties, mechanism of action, 
S.A.R. and metabolism of drugs dealt hereunder will also be emphasized. Special emphasis will be laid on 
drug discovery, drug design and related topics.

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1. Course Description: 
This course is a laboratory oriented course and covers instrumentation and applications of various analytical techniques 
such as UV-visible, Infrared, NMR spectroscopy, Mass spectrometry etc for drug discovery and  development 
 
2. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
The course is aimed at exposing the students to modern analytical techniques in relevance to pharmaceutical 
industries. Training with respect to the operation of sophisticated instruments, interpretation of results obtained for 
the characterization of molecules, their qualitative and quantitative evaluation are emphasized. 
Objectives 
 Exposure to principles, instrumentation, calibration and operation of analytical instruments  
 Obtaining spectral data, their interpretation, evaluation of qualitative and qu antitative aspects of 
drugs and their estimation

syllabus.heading: Course description

sources.text:
1. Course description: Physical, chemical, and biopharmaceutical considerations in formulations, absorption, 
distribution, and elimination of drugs; pharmaceutical additives; formulation, manufacturing, packaging, 
quality control, and stability of solid dosage forms, semi -solid dosage forms, liquids dosage forms, and 
sterile preparations including parenteral suspensions, emulsions, depot formulations; microencapsulation 
and controlled release formulations; targeted drug delivery systems; multi -unit particulate systems; 
transdermal, gastroretentive, and nasopulmonary drug delivery systems; aerosol products and packaging. 
2. Scope & Objective of the Course:  It is a course intended to give students insight into the problems 
involved in making drug dosage forms . It brings together the various sciences involved in developing 
pharmaceutical product formulations and evaluating their quality. The laboratory component involves some 
fundamental exercises in the evolution of products such as tablets, ointments, solutions, parenteral products, 
sustained-action medications, etc. It also imparts knowledge of newer dosage forms.

Course Title               :  QUALITY ASSURANCE & REGULATORY AFFAIRS

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
Course Description:  
Quality control, assurance and management, various parameters for achieving quality 
pharmaceutical products, application of statistics in quality assurance, reliability, cGMP for 
pharmaceutical manufacturing , pharmaceutical process validation, drug regulatory af fairs, clinical 
research protocols, new drug applications. 
1. Scope and Objective of the course: 
This course deals with the basic need of quality in the manufacturing of Pharmaceutical products 
and it's build up with the help of quality control and quality assurance management. Various 
current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) to be followed in a pharmaceutical organization and 
its validation procedure are part of the course. This course also covers the regulatory procedures 
applicable in clinical trials and approval of new drug products. 
2. Text Book (T): 
T1: Sidney H. Willig, Murray M. Tuckerman and William S. Hitchings IV, " Good Manufacturing 
Practices for Pharmaceuticals: A Plan for Total Quality Control" Marcel Dekker, New York, 
4th  Edn., Vol. 78, 1997. 
T2: Bernard T. Loftus and Robert A. Nash, " Pharmaceutical Process Validation" Marcel Dekker, 
New York, 2nd Edn., Vol. 57, 1993. 
Reference Books (R): 
R1: Richard A. Guarino, " New Drug Approval Process" Marcel Dekker, New York,     2 nd Edn., Vol. 
56, 1993. 
R2: Dale H. Be sterfield, “Quality Control”Prentice Hall International Inc., New Jersey, 5 th Edn., 
1998. 
R3: Sandy Weinberg, “Good Laboratory Practices’ Marcel Dekker, New York,     2 nd Edn., Vol. 69, 
1995. 
R4: Leon Lachman, Herbert L. Lieberman and Joseph L. Kanig " The Theory and Practice of 
Industrial Pharmacy" Varghese Publn., Bombay, 3rd Edn., 1987.  
R5: U.S. Pharmacopeia, U.S. Pharmacopeial Convention Inc., Rockville, MD, 23rd Edn., 1995.

Course Title : Separation and Structure Elucidation Techniques

syllabus.heading: Course Description

sources.text:
1.  Course Description: Advance separation methods for complex Natural, Semi -synthetic and Synthetic 
New Chemical Entities (NCEs) using LC -MS, LC-MS-MS, LC-NMR, GC-MS, GC-MS-MS, CE-MS, 
Supercritical Fluid Chromatography. Structure elucidation of NCEs using 2D, 3D ( 1H and 13C) NMR 
spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction technique. Prediction of structures using Software tools.

instructors.label: Instructor-in-Charge
names: methods to identify immune react ions
ways to manipulate the immune system
immune responses in the context of infection
clinical immunology to promote lifelong learning

sources.text:
Instructor-in-Charge     :  Aniruddha Roy 
 
1. Scope and Objective of the Course: 
      This course covers key immunologic concepts: how the components of the immune system are generated, 
organized, and function; the mechanisms that lead to beneficial immune responses, immune disorders, and 
immunodeficiencies; methods to identify immune react ions; and ways to manipulate the immune system and its 
components to benefit the patient. This course will give the students an advanced understanding of the principles and 
mechanisms of the immune system and immune responses in the context of infection, malignancy and immunological 
disorders. The course will also enable the students to describe the fundamental mechanisms underlying immunologic 
disease and associate these mechanisms with strategies for therapeutic modulation of the immune system. It will help 
the students to gain the necessary transferable and research skills in basic and clinical immunology to promote lifelong 
learning and career development.
